flawed_step: The claim that triangle-freeness forces chromatic number at most 3 is false; triangle-free graphs can have arbitrarily large chromatic number (Mycielski construction).
counterexample: Grötzsch graph (Mycielskian of C5): vertices u1..u5 forming a 5-cycle (ui~ui+1 mod 5); w1..w5 with wi adjacent to u(i-1), u(i+1); z adjacent to all wi. 11 vertices, 20 edges. Triangle-free: C5 has no triangle; w's are pairwise nonadjacent; wi's u-neighbours u(i-1),u(i+1) are nonadjacent; z's neighbours (the w's) are independent. Not 3-colourable: if c is a proper 3-colouring with c(z)=3, all wi are in {1,2}; recolour each ui with c(ui)=3 to c(wi). This gives a proper 2-colouring of C5, because for adjacent ui,uj with c(ui)=3, wi~uj gives c(wi)≠c(uj). That is impossible for an odd cycle. So chromatic number is 4.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The Grötzsch graph is triangle-free (checked case by case) and has chromatic number 4 (a 3-colouring would turn into a 2-colouring of C5).
